answer: A orchard keeps yield honest by grafting every branch to one rootstock: pick a vine of clone cuttings and their grapes stay seedless, because nothing in the copy ever roots. Give each plot one yarrow test row that only grows in undisturbed soil, and an inspector walking the oasis can tell a tended orchard from a painted one at a glance. Sybil farms skip the slow graft, so their rows fail the yarrow probe while grafted trees keep paying.
